Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage overnight is dominated by the fallout from the US midterms colliding with an AI stock selloff — markets lurched from a historic post-election rally to a historic rout on fears Democratic control of Congress could slow data-center buildout, before partially rebounding Friday. Outlets are also converging on the strong October jobs report, Tesla's Cybertruck wind-down, and a wave of AI-industry corporate moves (Anthropic's IPO math, Microsoft-Oracle, OpenAI's data-center pledges).

stories.headline: AI stock rout followed by partial rebound after Democratic midterm sweep
stories.summary: Chipmakers and AI-linked stocks staged a historic one-day rally after the Democratic midterm sweep, then suffered an even bigger rout the next day on fears of tougher data-center regulation, before chip stocks began clawing back losses; Bloomberg described it as a chain reaction that took about 24 hours to turn negative after the election.

stories.headline: US economy adds 165,000 jobs in October, beating forecasts
stories.summary: October payrolls data showed the labor market adding jobs across industries and unemployment falling, reinforcing a narrative of resilience even as inflation and AI-related disruption weigh on workers; the surprisingly strong print also revived bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike in December.

stories.headline: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production, shift focus to Cybercab
stories.summary: Elon Musk said Tesla will stop producing the Cybertruck in Texas by mid-2027 to make room for its autonomous Cybercab ride-share vehicle, after the polarizing truck failed to reach mass-market sales despite several recalls.

stories.headline: Major investors skeptical Anthropic IPO can hit $1.5 trillion valuation
stories.summary: Institutional investors are pushing back on Anthropic's IPO price target amid the broader tech selloff, even as the AI company reported tripling revenue and disclosed roughly $895 billion in long-term compute commitments.

stories.headline: Microsoft winding down Oracle deal to rent AI cloud capacity
stories.summary: Microsoft is unwinding an arrangement to rent AI computing capacity from Oracle as part of a broader reassessment of its cloud partnerships, according to people familiar with the matter.

stories.headline: OpenAI pledges changes to data-center operations after midterm backlash
stories.summary: OpenAI said it will study noise impacts and report water use among other commitments for its data centers, and is urging lawmakers to adopt similar industry-wide standards following voter backlash over AI infrastructure in the midterms.

stories.headline: Fox closes $22 billion deal to buy Roku
stories.summary: Fox completed its $22 billion acquisition of Roku, a deal the Washington Post says will give Fox a significant edge in free, ad-supported streaming.

stories.headline: Wendy's rejects $1.4 billion takeover proposal from Nelson Peltz's Trian
stories.summary: Wendy's turned down a $1.4 billion takeover bid from activist investor Nelson Peltz's Trian, arguing the offer undervalues gains from its turnaround strategy.

Business.gaps: Business Insider and Politico had no business/markets-specific coverage found in the last 24-48 hours beyond general midterm-politics items that fell outside this group's topic; Puck's available items were focused on media, fashion, and Washington politics rather than core business/markets news.

US politics.overview: US political outlets are almost entirely consumed by the fallout from Tuesday's historic Democratic midterm sweep: the abrupt White House staff shakeup, Republican soul-searching and 2028 positioning, and the immediate policy and legal consequences of Democrats retaking Congress. A secondary thread involves investor and industry anxiety over AI following the election results, plus ongoing DOJ departures and court fights over Trump administration actions.

stories.headline: Trump Replaces Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as Chief of Staff
stories.summary: Trump is swapping out his longest-serving chief of staff for hardliner Stephen Miller, a move Axios frames as the president replacing a moderating force with 'one of the most maximalist champions of his agenda' after the midterm losses he blamed on Wiles.

stories.headline: Democrats' Midterm Wave Exceeded Even Their Own Expectations
stories.summary: House Majority PAC's president said the scale of Democratic gains landed 'on the very high end' of what the group had projected, underscoring how thoroughly the party outperformed forecasts.

stories.headline: Republicans Panic as Midterms Blow Open the 2028 Map
stories.summary: Strategists from both parties now view Ohio, Texas and Iowa as plausible 2028 battlegrounds after Democratic breakthroughs there, a dramatic shift from the traditional electoral map.

stories.headline: Judge Halts Construction of Trump's Triumphal Arch
stories.summary: Hours after a federal panel approved the project, a judge issued an overnight order blocking construction of Trump's planned arch for 14 days.

stories.headline: White House Cancels Tech Industry Panel After Anti-AI Midterm Backlash
stories.summary: The administration scrapped a planned meeting of top AI executives including Zuckerberg and Huang following the midterm results, as markets separately absorbed a $2.5 trillion tech selloff tied to fears of greater AI oversight under a Democratic Congress.

stories.headline: DOJ Shake-Up Continues With More High-Level Resignations
stories.summary: National security division chief John Eisenberg and Miami U.S. Attorney Jason Reding Quiñones resigned a day after Harmeet Dhillon's departure, deepening turmoil at the Justice Department.

stories.headline: No One Knows How Many Ballots Are Outstanding in Mississippi's Senate Race
stories.summary: The razor-thin contest between GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democrat Scott Colom is exposing how slow and decentralized Mississippi's vote-counting process is, leaving control of a pivotal Senate seat unresolved.

stories.headline: Democrats Won Congress. What Does That Mean for the Supreme Court?
stories.summary: SCOTUSblog examines how a Democratic-controlled Congress could reshape the court's trajectory, oversight posture, and future confirmation fights after Tuesday's results.

US politics.gaps: No distinct, recent (last 24-48h) stories could be confirmed directly from NOTUS or Cook Political Report; available material from both was dated well before the midterms. Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian coverage reflects only the feed items provided, as these outlets could not be searched directly.

Tech & AI.overview: Tech and AI coverage this week is dominated by fallout from the US midterms — a historic Democratic sweep that triggered a steep AI-stock selloff, a near-unanimous voter rejection of new data centers, and fresh doubts about Anthropic's roughly $1.5 trillion IPO valuation. Alongside the market turmoil, outlets are covering OpenAI's new offensive cybersecurity model GPT-6 Cyber, a METR audit suggesting Anthropic's AI-driven R&D has sharply accelerated, Congressional scrutiny of Nvidia's Jensen Huang over China ties, and the end of Tesla's Cybertruck.

stories.headline: Major investors skeptical Anthropic's IPO can hit $1.5 trillion valuation
stories.summary: Institutional investors are pushing back on Anthropic's targeted $1.5 trillion IPO valuation amid a broader tech selloff, with some suggesting the figure could land closer to $1 trillion.

stories.headline: AI-fueled stock rout deepens after Democrats' midterm sweep
stories.summary: Asian and European markets followed a US tech rout after Democrats' decisive midterm win stoked fears of a slower AI buildout, with the selloff compounded by a near-unanimous voter backlash against local data centers nationwide.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, a model built to find and patch vulnerabilities
stories.summary: OpenAI's company announcement introduces GPT-6 Cyber as a specialized security model for finding exploitable vulnerabilities and proposing fixes; VentureBeat reports the model already uncovered dozens of previously unknown Firefox flaws and is priced above rival cyber models from Anthropic and Google.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang summoned by Congress over China espionage concerns
stories.summary: Lawmakers want Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to answer questions about his alleged ties to a Chinese intelligence asset, adding to scrutiny of the chipmaker's China dealings.

stories.headline: METR finds Anthropic's AI research pace may have crossed its own acceleration threshold
stories.summary: After an eleven-week audit of Anthropic's internal data, nonprofit METR concluded that the pace of Claude model development has roughly doubled, with AI use within Anthropic driving about 80 percent of the speedup.

stories.headline: Tesla ends Cybertruck production, pivots to Cybercab
stories.summary: Tesla will stop Cybertruck production in mid-2027 to make room for its autonomous Cybercab ride-share vehicle, Elon Musk said, closing the book on a polarizing product that never seriously challenged the Ford F-150.

stories.headline: Meta abandons controversial AI training terms for Facebook pages
stories.summary: Meta backed off a planned update that would have forced Facebook page owners to allow AI training on linked content, after widespread criticism from creators.

stories.headline: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling even as usage climbs
stories.summary: New Ramp data indicates corporate AI spending has plateaued even as usage keeps rising, as price cuts and tighter cost controls among big spenders complicate investor assumptions about AI hypergrowth just as Anthropic nears its IPO.

Tech & AI.gaps: Platformer, The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist, The Guardian, IEEE Spectrum and Google DeepMind had limited or no distinctly new AI-industry-specific items beyond what's cited above within the last 24-48 hours; Platformer's latest dispatch (Nov 5) was used only via search since it blocks deeper crawling.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are dominated by fallout from this week's U.S. midterm elections, which are being read as a turning point for energy and data-center politics, alongside the run-up to the COP31 climate summit opening in Antalya on November 9. Utility-sector outlets are separately tracking a wave of Q3 earnings calls in which major utilities reaffirmed or expanded massive capital spending plans tied to data-center demand growth.

stories.headline: Trump's Energy Revolution Is Over. Now a New Era Begins.
stories.summary: Heatmap argues the midterm results mark the end of the Trump administration's anti-renewables push and the start of a new energy politics in which Democrats embrace 'every kind of energy source except for coal' while quietly reviving clean-energy tax credits and transmission buildout.

stories.headline: In a Divided World, COP31 Aims for Agreement on Electrification
stories.summary: Ahead of the COP31 summit opening November 9 in Antalya, organizers say a key measure of success would be a global commitment to raise electricity's share of final energy demand to 35% by 2035 from about 20% today, though the goal remains voluntary so far.

stories.headline: Exclusive: New Modeling Finds Permitting Bill Would Likely Cut Emissions
stories.summary: A new Rhodium Group analysis shared with Heatmap finds the bipartisan permitting bill (BAAJA) would likely cut U.S. emissions slightly and lower electricity bills by 2040, and would not increase emissions even in a worst-case scenario.

stories.headline: Voters just proved how much they hate data centers
stories.summary: Latitude Media reports that midterm results showed widespread voter backlash against data centers, a theme also explored in its piece on how Democratic governors who ran on ratepayer-defense messaging now have to govern on the issue.

stories.headline: Duke Energy to stay course on data center-fueled growth plan after 'historic' election
stories.summary: Duke Energy says its 15.4 GW large-load pipeline and $103 billion spending plan focused heavily on new natural gas capacity remain unchanged despite the midterm election results, while Sempra separately expects Oncor's capital plan to grow 20% on load growth even as its CEO says it's too early to gauge the election's impact.

stories.headline: DTE expands investment plan 30%, will sell unregulated subsidiary to fund growth
stories.summary: DTE is selling its unregulated DTE Vantage subsidiary for $3 billion and expanding its five-year electric investment plan by 30% as it repositions itself as what its CEO called a 'higher growth premium utility.'

stories.headline: Entergy sees progress on Arkansas data center deal, strong Q3 sales
stories.summary: Entergy's CEO reported strong third-quarter sales and progress on an Arkansas data center deal, while the company separately signed firm pipeline contracts for enough natural gas to support ten new combined-cycle power plants in Louisiana.

stories.headline: China's quarterly CO2 falls 3% in largest drop since Covid
stories.summary: Carbon Brief analysis finds China's CO2 emissions fell 3.1% in the third quarter of 2026, the sharpest quarterly drop since the Covid pandemic, amid continued fallout from the Hormuz crisis.

Energy.gaps: Canary Media's website showed no distinct news stories from the last 48 hours (only event/newsletter promotion pages); E&E News's recent search results were from months ago since its coverage has moved to Politico Pro, so no current E&E items could be confirmed. Reuters, FT, WSJ, NYT, The Economist and Argus Media block web search and had no feed items provided, so their current energy coverage could not be assessed.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage is dominated by countdown to the Trump-Xi summit at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen (Nov 18-19), with friction over rare earths and the looming Nov 10 Busan trade-truce deadline, alongside a global AI-stock selloff that hammered Taiwan's market and the fallout from Hong Kong and Macau national-security sentencings of pro-democracy figures. Business-focused outlets are also tracking Beijing's moves to stabilize its currency and stock market and China's fast-moving AI model race.

stories.headline: US-China trade chiefs talk ahead of Trump-Xi summit as Washington presses on rare earths
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer held a video call with Chinese Vice-Premier He Lifeng to finalize preparations for the Trump-Xi summit in Shenzhen, even as Washington publicly presses Beijing to fully deliver on rare-earth and critical-mineral commitments from the Busan deal, whose terms expire around Nov. 10.

stories.headline: Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years, drawing foreign condemnation
stories.summary: Jailed Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 years after pleading guilty to colluding with foreign forces, with Hong Kong officials hailing the verdict while Five Eyes allies and other governments called it an unjust prosecution and urged an end to similar national security cases.

stories.headline: Taiwan's Taiex suffers record intraday plunge as TSMC hits limit-down amid global AI selloff
stories.summary: Taiwan's stock market plunged a record 3,737 points at the open and TSMC hit its daily limit-down, as a Wall Street selloff over AI data-center policy uncertainty after the US midterms spread to Asian markets, prompting officials to prepare stabilization-fund intervention.

stories.headline: China's central bank moves to stabilize markets and curb yuan's rally
stories.summary: The People's Bank of China is raising the forex deposit reserve requirement ratio from 4% to 6% for the first time since 2021 to cool a yuan rally, while separately cutting its stock buyback relending rate to 1% after banks sought over 200 billion yuan in quotas to support a slumping stock market.

stories.headline: US and EU revive China policy talks after two-year hiatus
stories.summary: The European Union and United States are reviving a dialogue on China policy that had stalled since Trump's return to office, according to people familiar with the planning, signaling renewed transatlantic coordination on Beijing.

stories.headline: Macau sentences ex-lawmaker to 12.5 years in territory's first national security trial
stories.summary: A Macau court sentenced former lawmaker and democracy campaigner Au Kam San to 12 years and six months for subversion and other offenses, marking the territory's first national security trial and extending the region's crackdown on dissent seen also in Hong Kong this week.

stories.headline: Apple's China AI partnership with Alibaba's Qwen off to a bumpy start
stories.summary: Apple Intelligence began beta testing in China this week with Alibaba's Qwen model powering select Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence features, a high-profile partnership that has faced a rocky development process.

stories.headline: Rare labor strike at Taiwan chip plant highlights worker unrest amid AI boom
stories.summary: Workers at a Micron facility in Taoyuan staged a rare strike demanding greater profit shares and better bonuses, exposing labor tensions beneath Taiwan's central role in the global AI chip rush.

China.gaps: No current (last 24-48h) China-specific coverage could be found via search for Xinhua, CGTN, China Daily, Yicai Global, Sixth Tone or Global Times (whose retrievable recent items were historical rare-earths pieces, not from this window); ChinaTalk's only recent feed item was a general US Senate roundup not specific to China.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Middle East outlets is dominated by the escalating Strait of Hormuz shipping crisis and fears that Trump could order major new strikes on Iran after his party's midterm defeat. Saudi Arabia's deepening military and financial ties with Syria, Yemen's worsening Houthi conflict, and Israel's post-election coalition maneuvering to unseat Netanyahu are also major threads, alongside human-rights scrutiny of Bahrain and the UAE's role in Sudan.

stories.headline: Iran says tankers struck in Hormuz amid fears of new US attack
stories.summary: Iranian forces reported multiple tankers and a tugboat catching fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting mines, while a seafarer was killed in a separate missile strike on a Greek-owned tanker in the Gulf, deepening fears that Washington could resume major strikes on Iran.

stories.headline: As Trump weighs Iran strikes, possible nuclear opening emerges
stories.summary: With Republicans suffering sweeping midterm losses, Washington is weighing whether to resume major military strikes on Iran even as a possible diplomatic opening emerges, with Iran's enriched uranium stockpile and inspector access cited as key sticking points.

stories.headline: Riyadh releases $400m to help rebuild Syria's essential sectors
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia signed a defense cooperation pact with Syria and released over $400 million in concessional loans for Syrian energy, housing and health infrastructure during President Ahmed al-Sharaa's second Riyadh visit in a month, as Damascus is also reported to be quietly providing Saudi forces with military advice amid Houthi attacks.

stories.headline: Houthis and Yemeni government blame each other for Taiz market attack that killed 30
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthis and the internationally recognized government traded blame after a deadly strike on a market in Taiz killed around 30 people, as fighting between the two sides intensifies alongside continued Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia.

stories.headline: Rights groups condemn Bahrain's largest mass trial of Shia clerics in history
stories.summary: Rights groups have condemned Bahrain's largest-ever mass trial of Shia clerics, with 60 facing prison after interrogations that campaigners say were marred by abuse.

stories.headline: Leaked UN report 'establishes conclusively' that UAE hired Colombian mercenaries for Sudan's RSF
stories.summary: A confidential UN report reviewed by MEE reportedly details the UAE's recruitment of Colombian mercenaries to fight alongside Sudan's paramilitary RSF, adding fresh scrutiny to Abu Dhabi's alleged role in the Sudan war.

stories.headline: Israel opposition touts progress ousting Netanyahu after U-turn on ultra-Orthodox
stories.summary: Israel's opposition says it is making headway in efforts to unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after one ultra-Orthodox-aligned leader dropped his veto on military draft-exemption demands, as coalition talks continue following last week's inconclusive election.

stories.headline: Israel's Economy Defied Three Years of War. Now the Bill Is Coming Due.
stories.summary: After three years of resilience despite war, Israel's incoming government faces difficult fiscal choices balancing a swollen military budget against continued growth, complicated by Trump's threats to curtail US aid.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: No recent, relevant coverage could be found from Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Haaretz, or Arabian Business in the available search results.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage is dominated by South Africa's local elections, where the ANC crashed to a historic low, alongside a major US trade blow as Washington stripped South Africa and Rwanda of AGOA benefits. Economic stories on Ethiopia's growth-versus-conflict dilemma, Kenyan IPO activity, and Nigerian fintech regulation also feature prominently, alongside security concerns in eastern DRC and Tanzania's post-trial political fallout.

stories.headline: ANC heads to worst-ever election result, polling around 32%
stories.summary: Partial results from South Africa's local elections show the ruling ANC on track for its weakest performance ever, continuing a multi-year decline even as it remains the largest party.

stories.headline: US strips South Africa and Rwanda of AGOA trade benefits
stories.summary: The Trump administration has formally excluded South Africa and Rwanda from AGOA over alleged trade barriers, corruption and security concerns, with South Africa set to lose preferential access from January 2027 even as economists argue the practical financial hit may be smaller than headlines suggest.

stories.headline: Tanzania's Tundu Lissu cleared of treason but jailed for inciting unrest
stories.summary: Opposition leader Tundu Lissu avoided a potential death sentence on treason charges but was sentenced to four years in prison for inciting unrest, a verdict critics say still exposes deep flaws in Tanzania's judicial process.

stories.headline: Ethiopia touts robust growth as conflict risks threaten reform agenda
stories.summary: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government is promoting strong growth and export figures under its Homegrown Economic Reform agenda even as renewed fighting in the north raises fears the gains could unravel.

stories.headline: Armed group kills at least 33 in North Kivu village amid Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: Locals blame the ADF, an armed group that pledged allegiance to ISIL in 2019, for a deadly raid on villages in eastern DRC's North Kivu province, compounding an active Ebola outbreak in the region.

stories.headline: Quick Mart IPO oversubscribed as Kenyan listings gain momentum
stories.summary: Kenya's second-biggest supermarket chain saw demand for its IPO shares exceed supply by nearly 23%, marking the country's second listing this year and signaling renewed investor appetite for Kenyan equities.

stories.headline: Namibia's president takes personal control of Dangote's $2.5bn fuel project
stories.summary: President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah is personally overseeing Dangote's fuel storage and regional pipeline investment, breaking her own rule against direct involvement to avoid losing another major project to bureaucratic delay.

stories.headline: China and Gabon deepen ties as Oligui Nguema visits Beijing
stories.summary: Xi Jinping welcomed Gabon's president for a state visit aimed at strengthening bilateral relations, part of China's continued courtship of African governments.

Africa.gaps: The Continent, Mining Weekly and TechCabal's broader agenda were seen only via general homepage listings rather than fresh dedicated reporting matching this beat's top stories; Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ returned no Africa-specific items in the provided feeds or accessible search results.

Media.overview: Coverage clusters around the media fallout from this week's US midterms and ongoing fights between publishers and tech platforms over AI. Outlets are also tracking Fox's completed $22 billion Roku acquisition, CBS News's internal turmoil over a Trump-targeted '60 Minutes' report, and new flashpoints in the news industry's battle with Meta and OpenAI over content and licensing.

stories.headline: CBS News staff accuse network brass of throwing journalists under the bus amid Trump attack on '60 Minutes'
stories.summary: Status reports that the Trump administration's attack on a '60 Minutes' report has triggered internal finger-pointing at CBS News, with staffers angry at how network leadership has handled the fallout.

stories.headline: Fox Corp. completes $22 billion acquisition of Roku
stories.summary: Fox has closed its $22 billion deal for Roku, folding it into Fox Digital Platforms alongside Tubi, Fox One and Red Seat Ventures, and in the process Tubi CEO Anjali Sud and Roku's ad chief Charlie Collier are both departing rather than joining the combined company.

stories.headline: New York Times adds 420,000 digital subscribers in three months
stories.summary: The New York Times posted strong digital subscriber growth in the latest quarter, with its CEO crediting 'human made journalism' and product experiences readers actively seek out.

stories.headline: What could the Times buy if OpenAI settles its copyright suit?
stories.summary: Puck's Dylan Byers reports that the New York Times's landmark copyright case against OpenAI and Microsoft is nearing a decisive phase, with lawyers expecting a settlement potentially worth more than a billion dollars that could fund further M&A for the company.

stories.headline: Meta pauses controversial new terms of service after publisher backlash
stories.summary: Meta has indefinitely delayed proposed commercial terms that would have let it scrape websites run through Meta Business accounts, saying it is pausing changes to 'get this right' after publisher pushback.

stories.headline: Russia's Novaya Gazeta shuts down under government pressure
stories.summary: CJR reports that the independent Russian paper Novaya Gazeta is ceasing operations after Russian authorities and security services forced its editorial team to stop work, though a new project aims to preserve its archive digitally.

stories.headline: NBC tops cable and network ratings for midterm election night
stories.summary: Nielsen figures show NBC News led primetime midterm coverage with 6.7 million viewers, ahead of ABC, Fox News, CNN and MS NOW, as overall election-night audience rose 23% from the last midterms.

stories.headline: USA Today Co. blames AI for revenue decline while also betting on it
stories.summary: USA Today's parent company reported a lackluster third quarter with a net loss and declining revenue, pointing to AI-driven disruption as a culprit even as it pursues AI tools as part of its turnaround strategy.

Media.gaps: No recent media-industry coverage could be confirmed for NYT, WSJ, FT or The Guardian, since no relevant feed items were supplied for them and they block web search.
